sense_problem: Model sentence is slightly unnatural: 'If I had a better memory' + 'would have remembered' is rare; most people say 'If I had a better memory, I'd have remembered' only informally. Option 1 is a plausible rival reading.

'(not / miss)' nearly gives the answer; level fine.
'(have)' gives the verb; 'should have' also correct (more formal).
Gap is ambiguous: 'we visit / (that) we should visit' also fit the sentence; the hint '(visit)' makes both -ing and 'we visit' possible. 'visiting' is the intended answer.
Several tenses fit; (start) is the only hint, and 'starts' is the timetable use. Wrong/other answers 'will start' are fully correct.
No hint at all: any result linker fits (open gap); 'so' with a comma is poor but 'so' without comma would be fine. Too open for a typed gap.
'wouldn't use' is also accepted by many speakers; 'not use' is American subjunctive.
'(go)' hints 'to go' but 'we should/could go' also correct.
No hint: 'if' (informal), 'when' and 'whether' all fit; 'when my boss gives me the week off' is perfectly correct and sensible.
